newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iran acted properly since verdict-Germany's Herzog.
newsitem.headline: Iran acted properly since verdict-Germany's Herzog.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog on Tuesday said Tehran had acted properly so far in containing protests at a Berlin court verdict which implicated Iran's leaders in political murders.
"They have protected the German embassy against protests in Tehran and calmed down the demonstrators," Herzog told German and Polish schoolchildren visiting him at his Bellevue palace in Berlin.

But Herzog said if the verdict was correct then there had been a serious infringement of international law. A Berlin court two weeks ago jailed an Iranian and three Lebanese for the 1992 murder of four Kurdish dissidents, and said Tehran's leaders had ordered the killings.
The judgment prompted the 15-nation European Union to abandon its "critical dialogue" policy with Iran and -- with the exception of Greece -- recall envoys for consultation.
Iran's leadership officially protested against the verdict. Thousands of people took to the streets in Tehran, and some tried to storm the German embassy.

Tehran's Interior Minister Ali Mohammad Besharati said on Tuesday that Germany was the real loser in its diplomatic row with Iran, and that the West was wrong to believe Iranians would be "intimidated through threats and pressure".
But Besharati repeated assurances Tehran was committed to protecting foreign residents "who can reside in Iran without any worries", Iran's official news agency IRNA quoted him as saying.

German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel has appealed for calm in European states. In conciliatory remarks on Sunday, he said a "pause for thought" was needed to consider how Germany and the rest of Europe should redefine relations with Tehran.
He is due to discuss the future shape of relations with Iran with his EU counterparts at a meeting on April 29.

The EU's "critical dialogue" had aimed to keeping lines of communication with Iran open in the face of a U.S. policy of isolating Tehran. The EU has been trying to promote pro-Western elements and human rights in the Islamic Republic.
